patch_description: The current implementation uses a single global MAD-of-diffs sigma for the snap threshold. On volatile, non-stationary series this is suboptimal: clean segments get over-snapped (destroying genuine dynamics and increasing lag error) while noisy segments get under-snapped (allowing spurious reversals). This edit computes a locally adaptive robust noise scale: rolling MAD of first differences of `x_smooth` over ±25-sample windows via `np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view` (fully vectorized, O(n), no Python loops, no added latency), then applies a 0.5x local-sigma snap threshold per sample. Noisy segments receive aggressive snapping (protecting against false reversals) while clean segments preserve their dynamics (reducing lag error). The 0.5 multiplier retains margin in responsiveness while biasing toward trend preservation. Edge samples fall back to the global MAD-of-diffs so no samples are dropped and array length is unchanged, keeping the pipeline shape-compatible. This directly targets the multi-objective tradeoff: local adaptivity lets the reversal penalty and lag error be optimized jointly rather than traded off against one global constant.
